With the consent of the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. Appellant has filed the present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 against the award dated 06.07.2023 passed by Member, MACT, Anuppur in MACC No.04/2021 seeking reduction of compensation amount.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that deceased being bachelor 1 1/2 should have been deducted for personal and living expenses.
Respondents No.2 and 3 being brothers of deceased and cannot be treated to be dependent of deceased.
Further, in view of age of the deceased (21 years), 40 % should be added as future prospects.
Further, Tribunal has awarded consortium to all the respondents and only mother of the deceased shall be entitled to receive consortium.

Further,
tribunal has added 10% towards consortium and loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Whereas in view of judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 2017 SCC Online 1270 only after three years, 10 % is to be given under the conventional heads.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 2017 SCC Online 1270
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Tribunal has also imposed penal interest at the rate of 9%, if compensation amount is not deposited within two months.

4. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that Tribunal has 3 MA-6075-2023 awarded just and proper compensation to the respondent and no interference is required in the findings of the Tribunal and the appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. In the instant case, deceased was bachelor at the time of the accident, which is clear from the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.
Therefore, in view of judgment passed by Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transportation AIR 2009 SUPREME COURT 3104, 1/2 is to be deducted for personal and living expenses.
